docstring: Let $r \geq 2$. Is it true that $e(n,r+1) - e(n,r) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?
references: [Er87] Erdős, P., _Some problems on finite and infinite graphs_. Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985) (1987), 223-228.
[RuSz78] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Szemerédi, E., _Triple systems with no six points carrying three triangles_. Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Vol. II (1978), 939-945.
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (r : ℕ),
    2 ≤ r →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos600.eFunction n (r + 1)) - ↑(Erdos600.eFunction n r)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
